examples.en: I eat. After that, I take a walk.

examples.ko: 먼저 손을 씻고, 그러고 나서 요리를 시작해요.
examples.en: First I wash my hands, and after that I start cooking.

examples.ko: 숙제를 끝냈어요. 그러고 나서 친구를 만났어요.
examples.en: I finished my homework. After that, I met my friend.

examples.ko: 친구가 사과했어요. 그러고 나서 어떻게 됐어요?
examples.en: Your friend apologized. What happened after that?

examples.ko: 샤워를 하고 그러고 나서 바로 잤어요.
examples.en: I took a shower and after that went straight to bed.

examples.ko: 은행에 들렀어요. 그러고 나서 시장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I stopped by the bank. After that, I went to the market.

explain: '그리고'보다 앞 일이 끝난 뒤에 이어진다는 순서가 더 분명해요. 말할 때는 '그러고는'이나 '그러고서'처럼 바꿔 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 집에 와서 샤워했어요. 그러고는 바로 잤어요.
phrases.en: I came home and showered. Then I went straight to bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 자주 쓰고, 앞 일에 바로 이어지는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in speech, with a feeling of following right after.

phrases.example: 숙제를 해요. 그리고 나서 게임을 해요.
phrases.en: I do my homework. After that, I play games.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그러고 나서'와 거의 같고 둘 다 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same, and both are very common.

phrases.en: After eating, I drink coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 문장을 하나로 이어서 한 문장으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to join two actions into one sentence.

explain_en: Compared with '그리고', it makes clearer that the next thing happens after the first one is done. In speech people also say '그러고는' or '그러고서' in its place.

examples.ko: 친구와 수다를 떨었어요. 그러다가 막차를 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: I was chatting with my friend. Then I missed the last train.
Don't overdo it. You'll get sick if you keep that up.
I was reading a book. Then I fell asleep.

examples.ko: 길을 걷고 있었어요. 그러다가 옛 친구를 만났어요.
examples.en: I was walking down the street. Then I ran into an old friend.

examples.ko: 처음에는 조용했는데 그러다가 갑자기 큰 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: It was quiet at first, but then suddenly there was a loud noise.

examples.ko: 계속 게임만 해요? 그러다가 시험에 떨어지면 어떡해요?
examples.en: You keep playing games only? What if you fail the exam like that?

explain: 하던 일이 계속되는 중에 다른 일이 생기거나 상태가 바뀔 때 써요. 걱정이나 경고를 할 때 '그러다가 ~면 어떡해요?'처럼도 자주 말해요. 줄여서 '그러다'라고 하기도 해요.

phrases.example: TV를 보다가 잠들었어요. 그러다 새벽에 깼어요.
phrases.en: I fell asleep watching TV. Then I woke up at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그러다가'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of the headword, common in speech.

phrases.example: 밤새 게임하면 안 돼요. 그러다가는 시험에 떨어져요.
phrases.en: Don't play games all night. If you keep that up, you'll fail the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속하면 나쁜 일이 생긴다고 경고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn that continuing will lead to a bad result.

phrases.example: 계속 연습하세요. 그러다 보면 잘하게 돼요.
phrases.en: Keep practicing. Before you know it, you'll get good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속하다 보면 결과가 생긴다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that if you keep going, a result will come.

explain_en: Use it when something else happens or the situation changes while the earlier action is continuing. It is also common in warnings, like '그러다가 ~면 어떡해요?' (What if ... happens if you keep doing that?). It can be shortened to '그러다'.

examples.en: I have studied Korean hard until now.

examples.ko: 처음부터 지금까지 이 약속을 지켜 왔어요.
examples.en: I have kept this promise from the beginning until now.

examples.ko: 고대 이집트의 벽화가 지금까지 선명하게 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Wall paintings from ancient Egypt remain vivid even now.
So far everything was fine, but I'm worried about from now on.
What on earth have you been doing from yesterday until now?
Teacher, thank you so much for helping me until now.

explain: 과거부터 말하는 지금까지 이어진 일에 써요. 비슷한 '이제까지'와 거의 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. '지금까지는 ~지만'처럼 '는'을 붙이면 앞으로는 다를 수 있다는 느낌이 생겨요.

phrases.en: I have never been late until now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지금까지'와 거의 같아요. 바꿔 써도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same; the two can be swapped.

phrases.en: It's been fine so far, but I don't know about from now on.
phrases.nuance_ko: '는'을 붙이면 앞으로는 다를 수 있다는 느낌이 생겨요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the topic particle hints that things may change from now on.

phrases.example: 저는 지금까지 계속 이 동네에서 살았어요.
phrases.en: I have lived in this neighborhood all the way until now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 이어진 일을 강조할 때 '계속'을 덧붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the word for 'continuously' stresses that something has gone on without a break.

explain_en: It refers to something that has continued from the past up to the present moment. It can be swapped with '이제까지' in most cases. Adding '는', as in '지금까지는 ~지만', suggests that things may be different from now on.

examples.en: I met a friend at the park last weekend.
Last Saturday was my grandmother's birthday.
I was really very busy last week.
I went on a trip to Busan last summer.
It is past midnight, so there is no subway.
I'll return the book I borrowed last time today.

explain: '지난'은 항상 명사 앞에 오는 말이에요. '지난주, 지난달, 지난해, 지난번'은 붙여 쓰고, '지난 주말, 지난 여름'처럼 다른 말 앞에서는 띄어 써요. 반대는 '다음'이나 '이번'이에요.

phrases.en: Last week I watched a movie with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지난'과 '주'를 붙여 쓰면 바로 앞의 한 주를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Written as one word, it means the week just before this one.

phrases.en: I moved to a new house last month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 앞의 달을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the month just before this one.

phrases.en: I brought the book I mentioned last time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 앞의 한 번을 말할 때 써요. 때가 정해져 있지 않아도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the previous occasion, without a fixed time.

explain_en: '지난' always comes before a noun. '지난주', '지난달', '지난해', and '지난번' are written together, while it is spaced in '지난 주말' and '지난 여름'. The opposites are '다음' (next) and '이번' (this).

examples.en: I eat lunch by myself.
You did the whole move by yourself? That's impressive.
I figured out how to ride a bike on my own.

examples.ko: 다섯 살 아이가 혼자서 옷을 입어요.
examples.en: The five-year-old child puts on clothes by himself.
Traveling alone is free, but sometimes lonely.

examples.ko: 이 상자는 너무 무거워서 혼자서는 못 들어요.
examples.en: This box is too heavy for me to lift by myself.

explain: '혼자'와 거의 같지만 '혼자서'는 도움 없이 직접 한다는 느낌이 조금 더 강해요. '혼자서는 못 해요'처럼 '는'과 같이 쓰면 힘들다는 뜻이 돼요. 둘이면 '둘이서', 셋이면 '셋이서'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I live alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼자서'보다 더 짧고 자주 쓰고, 다른 사람 없이 한 명이라는 사실을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter and more common; it simply states that no one else is involved.

phrases.example: 이 일은 너무 커서 혼자서는 못 해요.
phrases.en: This job is too big, so I can't do it by myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '는'을 붙여서 혼자라면 힘들다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the particle shows that doing it alone would be too hard.

phrases.en: My friend and I watched a movie, just the two of us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 둘일 때 쓰고, 셋이면 '셋이서'로 바꿔요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there are two people; change the number for three or more.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as '혼자', but '혼자서' puts a bit more emphasis on doing something without help. Adding '는', as in '혼자서는 못 해요', conveys that it is hard. For two people you say '둘이서', and for three '셋이서'.

examples.ko: 일반적으로 온라인 조사는 현장 조사보다 비용이 적다.
examples.en: Generally, online surveys cost less than on-site surveys.

examples.ko: 일반적으로 고객은 가격보다 서비스에 더 민감하게 반응해요.
examples.en: In general, customers react more sensitively to service than to price.

examples.ko: 일반적으로 신제품은 출시 직후에 판매량이 가장 많습니다.
examples.en: Generally, a new product sells the most right after launch.

examples.ko: 일반적으로는 그렇지만 이번 사례는 예외로 봐야 해요.
examples.en: That's true in general, but this case has to be treated as an exception.

examples.ko: 일반적으로 계약서는 양쪽이 서명한 날부터 효력이 생긴다.
examples.en: Generally, a contract takes effect from the day both sides sign.

explain: '일반적으로'는 전체를 두고 말할 때 쓰고, '개인적으로'는 내 생각을 따로 말할 때 써요. 그래서 '일반적으로는 그렇지만, 개인적으로는 달라요'처럼 짝으로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: 일반적으로 speaks about things as a whole, while 개인적으로 sets out your own view. So they can be paired: 일반적으로는 그렇지만, 개인적으로는 달라요 ('generally so, but personally I differ').

examples.ko: 학교 갔다 오면 숙제부터 하고 놀아야 해요.
examples.en: When you come back from school, you should do homework first and then play.

examples.ko: 우리끼리 여행이나 한번 갔다 오면 어떨까요?
examples.en: How about we go on a trip just the two of us and come back?

examples.ko: 잠깐 편의점에 갔다 올게요. 뭐 사 올까요?
examples.en: I'll go to the convenience store and be right back. Shall I buy anything?
I went to my parents' house and came back yesterday.
May I go to the restroom and come back?
I'll contact you after I get back from my business trip.

explain: '다녀오다'와 거의 같은 뜻인데, 집을 나설 때 인사는 '다녀올게요'라고 해요. 보내는 사람은 '다녀오세요'라고 말해요. 길게는 '갔다가 오다'라고도 하고, 말할 때는 '갔다 오다'를 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I went to Busan over the weekend and came back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갔다 오다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 인사말에도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same in meaning as the headword, and it is also widely used in greetings.

phrases.en: Mom, I'm off to school (and will be back).
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 나설 때 하는 인사로, 돌아오겠다는 뜻이 들어 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A greeting said when leaving home, which carries the promise of coming back.

phrases.en: I'll go to the bank and come back. Please wait.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갔다 오다'를 풀어서 말한 것으로, 두 동작을 나눠서 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spelled-out form of the headword, which treats the going and the returning as two separate steps.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '다녀오다', but the greeting when leaving home is '다녀올게요'. The person seeing you off says '다녀오세요'. The longer form is '갔다가 오다', and in speech '갔다 오다' is commonly used.

en: to be wide / to be spacious

examples.en: Our living room is spacious.
This park is really big.

examples.ko: 방이 넓어서 침대를 두 개 놓을 수 있어요.
examples.en: The room is spacious, so you can put two beds in it.

examples.ko: 넓은 주차장에 자동차가 한 대도 없어요.
examples.en: There isn't a single car in the big parking lot.

examples.ko: 저는 넓은 집보다 작은 집이 좋아요.
examples.en: I like a small house more than a big one.

phrases.nuance_ko: 인맥이 넓어요
phrases.nuance_en: describes someone with a wide circle of connections
phrases.en_equiv: to know a lot of people, to be well-connected

I have rice and soup every morning.
We eat soup with a spoon.

examples.en: How many people are in your family?
What time is it now?

examples.en: How many apples are there? — There are five.
How old is the child? — Seven.

examples.ko: 한국어 책이 몇 권 있어요? — 세 권 있어요.

examples.en: I bought water from the vending machine on the first floor.
I put coins in the vending machine.
I buy water from the vending machine in front of the convenience store.
